clue.text: Itchy feet of staff result in turmoil

parts.note: a wand is a rod or staff, as carried by an official or a magician

indicators.note: in turmoil says the letters of the word before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A walking staff, used too much, leaves a traveller with sore, restless feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itchy feet' looks literal but is the idiom for a restless urge to travel; 'staff' is a rod, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is the idiom for a restless longing to travel, the craving the German loanword names.

clue.text: Shrewd manner of the old

definitions.meaning: in archaic English the word meant way or manner

explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious and the archaic noun for a way of doing things share this spelling.

clue.text: Italian's ending with lots of pasta

indicators.note: ending picks out the final letter of the word Italian's

parts.note: oodles means lots, a great quantity

explanation.surface: An Italian finishes with plenty of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: These long strips of dough are a form of pasta, as in egg pasta.

clue.text: Pilot formerly mad about fairylike creature

indicators.note: about says the formerly and mad words go around the fairy

parts.note: ex- means formerly, as in ex-wife
mental is slang for mad
a peri is a fairy or elf in Persian mythology

explanation.surface: A one-time pilot has gone crazy over a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like a flyer but is an adjective, as in a pilot scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot project is a trial run, a test version of something.

clue.text: Means of avoiding a gap in the defences

definitions.meaning: a way of escaping a rule or obligation, as in a tax dodge
a narrow slit in a castle wall for shooting through

explanation.definitionFit: Both an ambiguity that lets one evade a law and an arrow slit in a fortification take this name.

clue.text: Excessively sentimental boy following girl out East

indicators.note: following means the boy's name comes after the shortened girl's
out says the East letter is removed from the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
E is the compass abbreviation for East
Gary is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A soppy boy trails after a girl heading out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl out East' reads as a girl travelling east, but 'out' is an instruction to drop the East letter from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-sweet, cloying sentiment is described with this word, as with saccharine.

clue.text: Head of chapter author's beginning in study

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study

indicators.note: the beginning of the word author's is its first letter only

explanation.surface: A cathedral's senior cleric starts writing a book from his study.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral chapter is its governing body of clergy, so its head is this cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: The cleric presiding over a cathedral chapter holds this title, so he is its head.

clue.text: Typical example I entered in the record book

indicators.note: entered in says the letter I goes inside the record and book combined

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a typical example of their entry in a record book.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitome of something is the perfect instance of it.

clue.text: Open to discussion, albeit gone haywire

indicators.note: gone haywire means out of control, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is still debatable even though it has spun out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms that can still be bargained over are said to be flexible in this way.

clue.text: Road clearer at present parking in Berkshire town

indicators.note: in tells us the present and parking letters sit inside the town's name

parts.note: Slough is a large town in Berkshire, the county west of London
now means at present
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Something clearing the road is currently parked in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOUGH is a town in Berkshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This vehicle pushes snow off highways, so it literally clears the road.

clue.text: Band used for Wagnerian operas

definitions.meaning: a plain circular band, as worn on a finger
Wagner's four-opera cycle about a cursed gold band is commonly called by this short title

explanation.definitionFit: A finger band is this ornament, and Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen gives the operas their nickname.

clue.text: As peer proved, possibly, one may overhear things in the upper house?

definitions.text: one may overhear things in the upper house?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A peer has proved that a member of the House of Lords can be overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AS PEER PROVED. 'upper house' looks like the Lords, but it is literally the house's eaves, under which a listener once stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who stands under the eaves to listen in, so a secret listener.

clue.text: Aspersion hanging over the music staff?

definitions.meaning: a slighting remark that damages someone's reputation
in notation a curved line drawn over notes on the stave shows they are played smoothly joined

explanation.definitionFit: A smear on someone's name is an insult of this kind, and the curved legato mark above notes shares the word.

clue.text: Male soldiers leading an attack in this vicinity

indicators.note: leading means the male and soldier letters come in front of the rest

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers
a bout is a fit or attack, as of illness

explanation.surface: Male troops spearhead an assault somewhere near here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an attack' reads as A BOUT, a bout being a spell of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old-fashioned adverb meaning nearby, around this place.

clue.text: Skill shown by crew member in charge of escape vessel

parts.note: a hand is a member of a ship's crew
a raft is a craft used to escape a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A sailor shows ingenuity when commanding a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft work, making things by hand, requires this kind of manual skill.

clue.text: Marshal with the power to encompass overthrow of state

indicators.note: to encompass says the word for power wraps around the turned state

parts.note: able means having the power to do something

indicators.note: overthrow of says the word for state is turned upside down, read backwards in an across entry

parts.note: a mess is a state, as in 'what a state the kitchen is in'

explanation.surface: A military marshal is empowered to bring about a coup against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like an officer's rank, but it is the verb meaning to gather; 'overthrow' works as a reversal here, not a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops is to gather them together, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Small amount of foreign money put into plant

indicators.note: into says the word for put goes inside the plant

parts.note: the pea is a climbing plant
set means put, as in 'set it down'

explanation.surface: A little foreign cash is invested in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a low-value unit of Spanish currency before the euro.

clue.text: Escort providing tea before Evita, perhaps?

indicators.note: before says the tea word comes ahead of the surname

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Eva Perón, nicknamed Evita, is an example of someone surnamed Perón

explanation.surface: A chaperone treats Evita to tea first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accompanies a young woman for propriety is an escort of this kind.

clue.text: Appropriate direction repeated by a governess

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate, as in 'due respect'

indicators.note: repeated says the direction letter appears twice

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A governess gives the proper instruction twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style chaperone or older woman in charge of girls, close to a governess.

clue.text: Day before disorderly clan enters San Marino, say

indicators.note: enters says the scrambled clan goes inside the day before

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters of clan are scrambled

explanation.surface: On the eve of a feast an unruly clan pours into San Marino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' turns CLAN into NCLA, which 'enters' puts in EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny state wholly surrounded by Italy, an example of such a territory.

clue.text: Abandon wickedness? Not this woman!

parts.note: split the answer into a phrase meaning give up evil, and note that a thoroughly malicious woman would never do so

explanation.surface: Someone urges reform, and is told this woman will never give up her wicked ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into SHED (abandon) and EVIL (wickedness), yet a woman of that kind is the last who would.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful, malicious woman is called a fiend of this sort.

clue.text: Governor's man turned up once long ago

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: Vic is a man's name

indicators.note: turned up says the word for long ago is read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: yore means long ago, as in 'days of yore'

explanation.surface: A governor's servant showed up in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns YORE into EROY. 'Governor's man' reads as a servant, but 'man' is VIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governing a colony on behalf of a monarch holds this title.

clue.text: Oppidan individual embraced by supporter on course

indicators.note: embraced by says the individual word goes inside the golf supporter

parts.note: a tee supports the ball on a golf course
own means individual or particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A town dweller gets a hug from a fan at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppidan is a rare word for a town dweller, also used at Eton. 'supporter on course' looks like a racing fan but is a golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidan means a town resident, as opposed to a country person or a student.

clue.text: Give a band a raise, being in very high spirits

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as a dog cocks its ear
a hoop is a circular band, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: An instruction to award a musical group a pay rise, which delights them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians, but it is a ring of metal; 'raise' is a verb, not a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exultant and elated is what this old idiom describes, as joyful as can be.

clue.text: Formerly part of graduation ceremonies

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Graduation ceremonies used to be something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at some time in the past, previously.

clue.text: Vain-sounding object of adulation

indicators.note: sounding says the word for vain is heard, not spelt

parts.note: vain means futile or useless, as is idle talk

explanation.surface: A conceited person is the object of everyone's adoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like conceited, but here it means futile, as idle threats are.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worshipped by fans is a pop star or similar figure, as a god is to believers.

clue.text: Horse a body of lawyers backed

indicators.note: backed says the word for lawyers is read in reverse

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers

explanation.surface: A horse is supported financially by a group of lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' suggests betting on a horse, but here it turns BAR into RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous breed of horse from the Middle East, prized for speed and stamina.

clue.text: Caught on the hop, peacekeepers quietly went without one

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: without says the numeral is dropped from the word for went

parts.note: repaired means went, as in 'repaired to the bar'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers were surprised, having moved off quietly without one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I from REPAIRED, leaving REPARED. 'Caught on the hop' is British slang for taken by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught on the hop means taken by surprise, not ready.

clue.text: Engineers refilling tank for long journey

indicators.note: refilling says the inside of the tank is emptied and the engineers fill it instead

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers refuel a tank before setting out on a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refilling' first empties the tank of its middle letters, then puts the engineers in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, arduous journey on foot is a synonym of the word.

clue.text: Mint's coin of exceptional quality

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a penny is a coin
royal means splendid, of exceptional quality, as in 'a royal feast'

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint produces a coin of the very finest quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the place coins are made, but it is the herb family.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant is a species of the herb genus Mentha.
